title: BMOPF network case schema 0.2.0

$schema.description: Schema retrieval URI or documented canonical identifier. A pinned proposal uses an immutable commit URL. Its resolved version must agree with meta.schema_version when both are supplied.

version.description: The version of this dataset, chosen by whoever publishes the case. Independent of `meta.schema_version`.

license.description: The licence the case data is published under, as an SPDX identifier where one exists, e.g. `CC-BY-4.0`. Network cases inherit the licence of the data they derive from; this schema's licence does not apply to them.

frequency.description: Nominal system frequency [Hz]. A line geometry's `frequency` and a linecode's `derivation.frequency` are checked against it. It defaults nothing and rescales nothing.

data_sources.description: Upstream data sources from which this case was derived

case_study_generator.description: Tool that generated this case file

provenance.description: Free-form conversion/audit provenance written by tooling (e.g. a fidelity-loss inventory, migration notes, or earth-terminal routing).

schema_version.description: The version of the schema document, fixed by that document. Distinct from `meta.version`, which versions the dataset.

extras.description: The one free-form object of the document: case-level data this schema does not define. Every other object rejects unknown fields. Data here carries no defined meaning, so a reader that ignores it reads a different network than the writer wrote.

terminal_names.description: Ordered array of terminal names for this bus

perfectly_grounded_terminals.description: Array of terminal names which are perfectly grounded

v_min.description: Minimum voltage magnitude [V] of each phase terminal of the bus, phase to ground, one entry per name in `terminal_names` that `terminal_conventions` classifies as a phase, in `terminal_names` order. The neutral bounds through `vn_max`, so this array carries no entry for it.

v_max.description: Maximum voltage magnitude [V] of each phase terminal of the bus, phase to ground, one entry per name in `terminal_names` that `terminal_conventions` classifies as a phase, in `terminal_names` order. The neutral bounds through `vn_max`, so this array carries no entry for it.

vn_max.description: Maximum neutral-to-ground voltage magnitude [V]; only valid when the bus has a neutral terminal

vpn_min.description: Minimum phase-to-neutral voltage magnitude [V], one entry per phase terminal in `terminal_names` order. Valid only when the bus carries a neutral terminal.

vpn_max.description: Maximum phase-to-neutral voltage magnitude [V], one entry per phase terminal in `terminal_names` order. Valid only when the bus carries a neutral terminal.

vpp_min.description: Minimum phase-to-phase voltage magnitude [V], one entry per ordered phase pair (1,2), (2,3), (3,1) of the bus's phase terminals, in that order. Valid only on a bus with at least two phase terminals.

vpp_max.description: Maximum phase-to-phase voltage magnitude [V], one entry per ordered phase pair (1,2), (2,3), (3,1) of the bus's phase terminals, in that order. Valid only on a bus with at least two phase terminals.

vneg_max.description: Maximum negative-sequence voltage magnitude [V] (three-phase buses); the lower bound is always 0

vzero_max.description: Maximum zero-sequence voltage magnitude [V] (three-phase buses); the lower bound is always 0

length.description: Line length [m]. Required with `linecode` (impedance = per-metre matrices x length); optional and purely descriptive when the line carries inline absolute matrices

linecode.description: Linecode of line (per-metre matrices). A line carries EXACTLY ONE impedance source: either this reference (+ length), or inline absolute R_series_/X_series_ matrices in Ohm

i_max.description: Current-magnitude limit [A] on each conductor of the line, one entry per name in `terminal_map_from`, in that order, applied at both ends. Overrides the referencing linecode's `i_max`.

s_max.description: Apparent-power limit [VA] on each phase conductor of the line, one entry per phase conductor in `terminal_map_from` order, applied at both ends. Overrides the referencing linecode's `s_max`.

^R_series_\\d+_\\d+$.description: Element of the TOTAL series resistance matrix of this line section [Ohm]. Units by location: linecode matrices are per metre, line matrices are absolute - never scaled by length

^X_series_\\d+_\\d+$.description: Element of the TOTAL series reactance matrix of this line section [Ohm]

^G_from_\\d+_\\d+$.description: Element of the TOTAL from-side shunt conductance matrix [S]

^G_to_\\d+_\\d+$.description: Element of the TOTAL to-side shunt conductance matrix [S]

^B_from_\\d+_\\d+$.description: Element of the TOTAL from-side shunt susceptance matrix [S]

^B_to_\\d+_\\d+$.description: Element of the TOTAL to-side shunt susceptance matrix [S]

v_magnitude.description: Voltage magnitude [V] the source holds at each of its terminals, phase to ground, one entry per name in `terminal_map`, in that order. A grounded terminal states 0.

v_angle.description: Voltage angle [rad] the source holds at each of its terminals, one entry per name in `terminal_map`, in that order.

cost.description: Linear active-power cost [$/kWh] of each phase conductor of the source, one entry per phase conductor in `terminal_map` order. The source is not special in the objective: a positive injection is an import, so a positive entry is the import price and an export is credited at the same price. A scalar is rejected. Absent, the source carries no objective term.

p_min.description: Minimum active power [W] delivered by each phase conductor of the source, one entry per phase conductor in `terminal_map` order.

p_max.description: Maximum active power [W] delivered by each phase conductor of the source, one entry per phase conductor in `terminal_map` order.

shunt.description: Passive shunt admittance elements, including grounding impedances

capacitor.description: Fixed (nameplate-rated) shunt capacitor banks. See the math and data model for the element definitions and the q_rated/v_nom conventions per configuration.

q_rated.description: Nameplate rated reactive power of the whole bank [var], delivered when the voltage across the capacitor element terminals equals v_nom. For WYE and DELTA this is the total across all three elements, not a per-element rating.

v_nom.description: Nameplate nominal voltage [V]: line-to-line for the three-phase configurations (both WYE and DELTA); for SINGLE_PHASE, the nominal voltage across the terminals of the individual capacitor element.

load.description: Load elements. p_nom/q_nom are the nominal active/reactive powers; the ZIP and exponential voltage-dependence models and their coefficients are defined in the math and data model.

p_nom.description: Nominal active power [W] of each sub-load. One entry per sub-load, in `terminal_map` order. A sub-load is one two-terminal power element of the load: a phase-to-neutral branch for WYE, the single terminal pair for SINGLE_PHASE, or one line-to-line branch for DELTA. The sub-load count is the phase conductor count for WYE, one for SINGLE_PHASE, and the phase pair count for DELTA.

q_nom.description: Nominal reactive power [var] of each sub-load. One entry per sub-load, in `terminal_map` order. A sub-load is one two-terminal power element of the load: a phase-to-neutral branch for WYE, the single terminal pair for SINGLE_PHASE, or one line-to-line branch for DELTA. The sub-load count is the phase conductor count for WYE, one for SINGLE_PHASE, and the phase pair count for DELTA.

model.description: Voltage dependence of the load (default CONSTANT_POWER); see the math and data model for the definitions.

v_nom.description: Nominal voltage [V] each sub-load's `p_nom` and `q_nom` is stated at: line to line for the three-phase configurations, and the voltage across the load terminals for SINGLE_PHASE. Required unless `model` is CONSTANT_POWER. One entry per sub-load, in `terminal_map` order. A sub-load is one two-terminal power element of the load: a phase-to-neutral branch for WYE, the single terminal pair for SINGLE_PHASE, or one line-to-line branch for DELTA. The sub-load count is the phase conductor count for WYE, one for SINGLE_PHASE, and the phase pair count for DELTA.

alpha_z.description: Active-power constant-impedance fraction of the ZIP model. The three active fractions sum to one, and so do the three reactive fractions. One entry per sub-load, in `terminal_map` order. A sub-load is one two-terminal power element of the load: a phase-to-neutral branch for WYE, the single terminal pair for SINGLE_PHASE, or one line-to-line branch for DELTA. The sub-load count is the phase conductor count for WYE, one for SINGLE_PHASE, and the phase pair count for DELTA.

alpha_i.description: Active-power constant-current fraction of the ZIP model. The three active fractions sum to one, and so do the three reactive fractions. One entry per sub-load, in `terminal_map` order. A sub-load is one two-terminal power element of the load: a phase-to-neutral branch for WYE, the single terminal pair for SINGLE_PHASE, or one line-to-line branch for DELTA. The sub-load count is the phase conductor count for WYE, one for SINGLE_PHASE, and the phase pair count for DELTA.

alpha_p.description: Active-power constant-power fraction of the ZIP model. The three active fractions sum to one, and so do the three reactive fractions. One entry per sub-load, in `terminal_map` order. A sub-load is one two-terminal power element of the load: a phase-to-neutral branch for WYE, the single terminal pair for SINGLE_PHASE, or one line-to-line branch for DELTA. The sub-load count is the phase conductor count for WYE, one for SINGLE_PHASE, and the phase pair count for DELTA.

beta_z.description: Reactive-power constant-impedance fraction of the ZIP model. The three active fractions sum to one, and so do the three reactive fractions. One entry per sub-load, in `terminal_map` order. A sub-load is one two-terminal power element of the load: a phase-to-neutral branch for WYE, the single terminal pair for SINGLE_PHASE, or one line-to-line branch for DELTA. The sub-load count is the phase conductor count for WYE, one for SINGLE_PHASE, and the phase pair count for DELTA.

beta_i.description: Reactive-power constant-current fraction of the ZIP model. The three active fractions sum to one, and so do the three reactive fractions. One entry per sub-load, in `terminal_map` order. A sub-load is one two-terminal power element of the load: a phase-to-neutral branch for WYE, the single terminal pair for SINGLE_PHASE, or one line-to-line branch for DELTA. The sub-load count is the phase conductor count for WYE, one for SINGLE_PHASE, and the phase pair count for DELTA.

beta_p.description: Reactive-power constant-power fraction of the ZIP model. The three active fractions sum to one, and so do the three reactive fractions. One entry per sub-load, in `terminal_map` order. A sub-load is one two-terminal power element of the load: a phase-to-neutral branch for WYE, the single terminal pair for SINGLE_PHASE, or one line-to-line branch for DELTA. The sub-load count is the phase conductor count for WYE, one for SINGLE_PHASE, and the phase pair count for DELTA.

gamma_p.description: Active-power voltage exponent of the exponential model. One entry per sub-load, in `terminal_map` order. A sub-load is one two-terminal power element of the load: a phase-to-neutral branch for WYE, the single terminal pair for SINGLE_PHASE, or one line-to-line branch for DELTA. The sub-load count is the phase conductor count for WYE, one for SINGLE_PHASE, and the phase pair count for DELTA.

gamma_q.description: Reactive-power voltage exponent of the exponential model. One entry per sub-load, in `terminal_map` order. A sub-load is one two-terminal power element of the load: a phase-to-neutral branch for WYE, the single terminal pair for SINGLE_PHASE, or one line-to-line branch for DELTA. The sub-load count is the phase conductor count for WYE, one for SINGLE_PHASE, and the phase pair count for DELTA.

p_min.description: Minimum active power [W] of each phase conductor, one entry per phase conductor in `terminal_map` order.

p_max.description: Maximum active power [W] of each phase conductor, one entry per phase conductor in `terminal_map` order.

q_min.description: Minimum reactive power [var] of each phase conductor, one entry per phase conductor in `terminal_map` order.

q_max.description: Maximum reactive power [var] of each phase conductor, one entry per phase conductor in `terminal_map` order.

s_max.description: Apparent-power rating [VA] of each phase conductor, one entry per phase conductor in `terminal_map` order, bounding the sum of squares of that phase's active and reactive power.

i_max.description: Current-magnitude limit [A] of each conductor of the generator: one entry per phase conductor in `terminal_map` order, and optionally one further trailing entry that bounds the neutral return current, which is the negated sum of the phase currents. So the array is one entry per phase, or one per phase plus one.

cost.description: Linear active-power generating cost [$/kWh] of each phase conductor, one entry per phase conductor in `terminal_map` order. A scalar is rejected.

i_max.description: Current-magnitude limit [A] of each conductor of the cross-section, one entry per matrix row, in matrix row order, applied at both ends of every line that references the linecode.

s_max.description: Apparent-power limit [VA] of each phase conductor of the cross-section, one entry per phase conductor, in matrix row order.

source.description: Origin of the impedance matrices, e.g. "geometry" (compiled from a line_geometry), "fem" (finite-element derived), "datasheet", "import"

line_geometry.description: Back-reference to the line_geometry this linecode was compiled from

derivation.description: Provenance of the impedance computation: method, earth parameters, defaults applied, tool version. Stamped by compile_linecode; free-form for external tools (e.g. FEM)

frequency.description: Frequency the matrices were computed at [Hz]

temperature.description: Conductor temperature the resistances were corrected to [degC]

shields_reduced.description: Cable shield/concentric-neutral subconductors internally reduced into equivalent conductors, e.g. ["cn:1"]

defaults_applied.description: Cross-defaults applied during compilation, e.g. ["gmr:acsr_40"] when GMR was derived from radius

tool_version.description: Version of the tool that produced the matrices

^R_series_\\d+_\\d+$.description: Element of the series resistance matrix [Ohm/m]

^X_series_\\d+_\\d+$.description: Element of the series reactance matrix [Ohm/m]

^G_from_\\d+_\\d+$.description: Element of the shunt conductance matrix [S/m]

^G_to_\\d+_\\d+$.description: Element of the shunt conductance matrix [S/m]

^B_from_\\d+_\\d+$.description: Element of the shunt susceptance matrix [S/m]

^B_to_\\d+_\\d+$.description: Element of the shunt susceptance matrix [S/m]

open_switch.description: Indicator of switch state, true if switch is open (nonconducting)

i_max.description: Current-magnitude limit [A] on each conductor of the switch, one entry per name in `terminal_map_from`, in that order. A closed switch is ideal: the two terminal voltages are equal conductor by conductor and the currents sum to zero; an open switch carries no current.

center_tap.description: Center tap transformer object, with a single-phase winding on the 'from' side and split winding on the 'to' side.

wye_delta.description: Wye-to-Delta transformer object, with series impedance defined on the wye-side

delta_wye.description: Delta-to-Wye transformer object, with series impedance defined on the wye-side

single_phase_autotransformer.description: Single-phase step voltage regulator modelled as an autotransformer (series + common winding sharing a node). The ratio is the fixed tap_ratio; regulator_type selects ANSI Type A or B.

open_delta_regulator.description: Monolithic three-phase open-delta regulator: two single-phase autotransformer windings connected line-to-line across the phase pairs implied by connection (ABBC/BCAC/CABA).

n_winding.description: General n-winding (3+) transformer as a winding-indexed list with pairwise short-circuit reactances. Winding 1 is the reference; the OPF/Ybus build a star/T-equivalent. WYE and DELTA windings are supported (a DELTA winding's v_nom is its line-to-line coil voltage; delta_roll selects the vector-group rotation).

transformer.description: Transformers and step-voltage regulators, grouped by subtype. A subtype fixes the winding count, the winding connections, and which impedance fields apply; the object key inside a subtype is the element id.

terminal_conventions.description: Case-wide classification of the terminal-name labels used across the AC buses into phase, neutral and earth-wire roles. When present it is the authority on which label is which, labels are matched exactly including case, the role lists are disjoint, and every per-phase array dimension in the document resolves against it. When absent a reader infers the roles: `n` or `N` is the neutral, `"4"` is the neutral when the bus terminal set is exactly `1`, `2`, `3`, `4`, and every other label is a phase. The label `"g"` is reserved for the common ground and is never a bus terminal. This block does not apply to `dc_bus`, which states its own pole roles.

phase.description: Terminal-name labels that denote a phase conductor (e.g. ["a","b","c"], or split-phase legs). A bus terminal in neither list is treated as a phase and W.CONV.TERMINAL_UNCLASSIFIED is raised.

neutral.description: Terminal-name labels that denote a neutral conductor (typically ["n"]). A bus is expected to carry at most one neutral terminal.

earth.description: Terminal-name labels that denote a dedicated earth/PE *wire* conductor. The ground reference itself stays implicit (grounding is modelled via grounding impedances / perfectly_grounded_terminals); this list captures only genuine earth-wire terminals and is empty for standard OpenDSS-derived cases.

ibr.description: Inverter-based resources: photovoltaic arrays, battery storage, static compensators, and generic sources interfaced to the AC network through a converter. Per-phase arrays have one entry per phase conductor, which is the number of `terminal_map` names classified as a phase, in `terminal_map` order.

s_max.description: Per-phase apparent-power nameplate ratings [VA]; one entry per phase conductor (length = terminal_map - 1)

i_max.description: Optional per-conductor converter current-magnitude limit [A]. FOUR_LEG: one entry per phase plus a recommended final entry for the neutral conductor (length = phases or phases+1; a phases-only vector leaves the neutral unrated and warns, as it may carry more than the phases under unbalance compensation). SINGLE_PHASE: length 1 or 2 (phase and return are the same current - length-1 is standardised to 2). THREE_LEG: one entry per conductor (no neutral). When present, reactive capability rolls off ~linearly with voltage instead of staying flat at s_max; the neutral entry bounds the sum of phase currents

p_avail.description: Available active power [W]; upper bound on dispatch for PV prime movers

p_min.description: Per-phase minimum active power [W]; one entry per phase conductor (length = terminal_map - 1). Negative indicates absorption (battery charging)

p_max.description: Per-phase maximum active power [W]; one entry per phase conductor (length = terminal_map - 1)

dc_link_coupled.description: True if the converter's phases share a single DC link, so the per-phase active powers are coupled by a net DC-side balance (sum of phase P bounded by [p_dc_min, p_dc_max]). Lets the converter circulate active power BETWEEN phases (e.g. a four-wire STATCOM balancing an unbalanced feeder) while net active power stays inside the DC bound. False (default) treats each phase independently

p_dc_min.description: Minimum net DC-side active power [W] when dc_link_coupled; sum over phases of P >= p_dc_min. 0 for a STATCOM (no active source); negative permits absorption (battery)

p_dc_max.description: Maximum net DC-side active power [W] when dc_link_coupled; sum over phases of P <= p_dc_max. 0 for a STATCOM; p_avail for curtailable PV

dc_bus.description: Optional reference to a dc_bus id. When present, the converter's DC port injects into that shared DC node (participating in its DC KCL) instead of an isolated private DC link - this is how converter stations / back-to-back SOPs / MVDC ties are formed (several IBRs sharing one dc_bus). When absent, dc_link_coupled retains its isolated-link meaning (p_dc_min/p_dc_max bound).

dc_terminal_map.description: DC terminals of the referenced dc_bus the converter's DC port spans (e.g. [pole, return], or [pole] with earth return). Required when dc_bus is set.

dc_control.description: DC-side control mode for a dc_bus-coupled converter: P (constant power, default), V (DC-voltage master holding dc_v_set), or droop (saturated V-P droop). Each connected DC island needs at least one V or droop converter, else the DC voltage is underdetermined.

dc_v_set.description: DC-voltage setpoint [V], pole-to-return, for dc_control=V (held exactly) or droop (reference voltage). Defaults to the dc_bus pole-to-return v_dc_nom when absent.

dc_p_ref.description: Droop reference active power [W] at dc_v_set (the converter's AC active power when v_dc_port = dc_v_set). Used only for dc_control=droop.

dc_droop.description: Droop coefficient k [V/W] for dc_control=droop: P = dc_p_ref + (v_dc_port - dc_v_set)/k, so the converter exports more as the DC-port voltage rises, saturated at the converter power limits. Larger k = softer droop.

dc_deadband.description: Optional half-width [V] of a dead-band around dc_v_set within which the droop holds P = dc_p_ref (no response to small DC-voltage deviations). Used only for dc_control=droop.

q_min.description: Per-phase minimum reactive power [var]; one entry per phase conductor (length = terminal_map - 1). Negative indicates absorption (default -s_max)

q_max.description: Per-phase maximum reactive power [var]; one entry per phase conductor (length = terminal_map - 1) (default s_max)

r_filter.description: Per-phase filter resistance Re(Z_filter) [Ohm]; length matches terminal_map minus 1

x_filter.description: Per-phase filter reactance Im(Z_filter) [Ohm]; length matches terminal_map minus 1

grid_forming.description: True for grid-forming (GFM) operation; false (default) for grid-following (GFL)

v_ref_internal.description: Internal voltage magnitude setpoint [V]; grid-forming only

cost.description: Linear active-power dispatch cost [$/kWh] of each phase conductor, one entry per phase conductor in `terminal_map` order. The objective sums this rate against the active power the phase injects into the network, so a positive entry minimises injection and a negative entry maximises it. A scalar is rejected.

control_profile.description: Reference to a control_profile id encoding smart-IBR control laws

voltage_aggregation.description: Cross-phase aggregation of the droop monitored voltage for a multi-phase IBR: PER_PHASE (default, each phase reacts to its own magnitude) or AVERAGE (every phase reacts to the mean phase magnitude). When present it overrides the per-phase/averaged aggregation implied by a control law's voltage_reference.

control_profile.description: Optional IBR extension: reusable control-law profiles referenced by IBRs (linecode-style sharing). Each sub-object is optional; its presence activates the corresponding control law.

additionalProperties.description: A named control profile. Each control-law object is optional and its presence activates that law. Unknown control-law names are rejected.

volt_var.description: Volt-VAr droop: reactive power as a piecewise-linear function of a monitored voltage magnitude

breakpoints.description: The four voltage breakpoints [U1, U2, U3, U4] [V] of the droop, non-decreasing. Below U1 the converter injects `q_limits[1]`, between U2 and U3 it exchanges no reactive power, above U4 it absorbs `q_limits[0]`, and it interpolates linearly on [U1, U2] and [U3, U4].

q_limits.description: The two reactive-power limits [q_absorb, q_inject], q_absorb not positive and q_inject not negative, in vars or as a fraction of `s_max` as `q_unit` states.

p_min_for_q.description: Active power below which reactive output is zero (OpenDSS %PminNoVars)

p_min_for_q_max.description: Active power below which reactive capability is derated (OpenDSS %PminkvarMax)

volt_watt.description: Volt-Watt droop: active power limit as a piecewise-linear function of a monitored voltage magnitude

breakpoints.description: The two voltage breakpoints [U5, U6] [V] of the active-power limit, non-decreasing. At or below U5 the limit is `p_limits[0]`, at or above U6 it is `p_limits[1]`, and it interpolates linearly between them.

p_limits.description: The two active-power limits [p_low, p_high] reached at U5 and U6, in watts or as a fraction of the `p_ref` base as `p_unit` states.

pf.description: Power factor; positive = lagging (Q absorption), negative = leading (Q injection)

wire_data.description: Conductor and cable type library: construction data with no geometry, referenced by a `line_geometry` conductor. Resistance in Ohm/m, lengths in m, current in A, temperature in degC.

kind.description: Conductor construction: bare overhead round wire, concentric-neutral cable, or tape-shield cable

r_dc.description: DC resistance per unit length at temperature_ref [Ohm/m]. At least one of r_dc/r_ac is required (checked in the Julia layer); the other defaults via r_ac = 1.02 r_dc

r_ac.description: AC resistance per unit length at power frequency and temperature_ref [Ohm/m]

alpha_20.description: Temperature coefficient of resistance at 20 degC [1/K] for temperature correction, e.g. 0.00393 (Cu), 0.00403 (Al)

gmr.description: Geometric mean radius of the (phase) conductor [m]. At least one of gmr/radius required; the other defaults via gmr = 0.7788 radius (solid round)

radius.description: Physical outside radius of the (phase) conductor [m]

cap_radius.description: Electrostatic (capacitance) radius [m]; defaults to radius. Distinct field so bundled conductors can use an equivalent radius

i_max.description: Continuous current rating of the conductor [A]

eps_r.description: Relative permittivity of the cable insulation (cables only); OpenDSS default 2.3

d_strand.description: Diameter of one concentric-neutral strand [m] (cn_cable only)

gmr_strand.description: GMR of one concentric-neutral strand [m] (cn_cable only); defaults to 0.7788 d_strand/2

r_strand.description: Resistance per unit length of one concentric-neutral strand [Ohm/m] (cn_cable only)

d_shield.description: Diameter over the tape shield [m] (ts_cable only)

tape_lap.description: Tape shield overlap [percent] (ts_cable only); OpenDSS default 20

line_geometry.description: Line and cable cross-section assemblies: conductor types from `wire_data` placed at coordinates, each carrying one circuit terminal. A geometry compiles to a linecode. Every conductor carries a terminal, so the compiled matrix is the full primitive matrix at the stated conductor count and no conductor is eliminated; grounding stays on the bus, in `perfectly_grounded_terminals` and in shunts.

conductors.description: Ordered conductor placements. Position i fixes row and column i of the compiled linecode's matrices, and `terminal` names the circuit terminal conductor i carries.

x.description: Horizontal coordinate of the conductor centre [m]

y.description: Vertical coordinate of the conductor centre [m]; positive above ground, negative = burial depth

terminal.description: Circuit terminal this conductor carries, e.g. "a", "b", "c", "n"

earth_model.description: Earth-return formulation; default modified_carson (Kersting two-term). Note OpenDSS defaults to deri

frequency.description: Frequency the linecode is compiled at [Hz]. Required - there is no ambient default and no rescaling; the value is recorded in the compiled linecode's derivation block

temperature.description: Conductor operating temperature [degC]; resistances are corrected from wire_data temperature_ref using alpha_20 when present

dc_bus.description: Collection of DC buses (nodes of an MVDC/LVDC network). DC voltage is a signed magnitude relative to earth - no angle. A 1- or 2-terminal dc_bus is a monopole, a 3-terminal dc_bus is a bipole (positive pole, negative pole, metallic return). DC extension (all dc_* objects): under Task Force review for the July release.

terminal_names.description: Ordered DC terminal names. Length 1 (single pole, earth return), 2 (pole + return), or 3 (bipole: positive pole, negative pole, metallic return).

perfectly_grounded_terminals.description: DC terminal names held perfectly at earth potential (v_dc = 0). Same idiom as the AC bus.

pole.description: Optional map from terminal name to its pole role (POSITIVE, NEGATIVE, or METALLIC_RETURN), used for sign checks and line-to-line/line-to-neutral bound interpretation.

v_dc_nom.description: Per-terminal SIGNED nominal line-to-ground voltage [V] (positive pole > 0, negative pole < 0, return ~ 0). Used to derive v_dc_min/v_dc_max during augmentation when those are absent. One entry per name in `terminal_names`, in that order.

v_dc_min.description: Per-terminal SIGNED line-to-ground voltage lower bound [V]; one entry per terminal. Negative for a negative pole. One entry per name in `terminal_names`, in that order.

v_dc_max.description: Per-terminal SIGNED line-to-ground voltage upper bound [V]; one entry per terminal. One entry per name in `terminal_names`, in that order.

vdc_ln_min.description: Minimum line-to-neutral DC voltage magnitude [V] (pole minus return / metallic-return conductor). Requires a return/neutral terminal.

vdc_ll_min.description: Minimum line-to-line DC voltage magnitude [V] (positive pole minus negative pole). Bipole only.

vdc_ll_max.description: Maximum line-to-line DC voltage magnitude [V]. Bipole only.

dc_branch.description: Collection of DC lines/cables. Each branch is a multi-conductor (1/2/3-wire) link between two dc_bus nodes with per-conductor scalar resistance (no inter-conductor mutual coupling).

terminal_map_from.description: DC terminals of dc_bus_from this branch connects to; length = wire count (1/2/3).

terminal_map_to.description: DC terminals of dc_bus_to this branch connects to; same length as terminal_map_from.

r.description: Per-conductor resistance [Ohm]; one entry per wire. One entry per name in `terminal_map_from`, in that order.

i_max.description: Optional per-conductor current-magnitude limit [A]. One entry per name in `terminal_map_from`, in that order.

dc_grounding.description: Collection of DC earthing/return points. r = 0 (or omitted) is perfect grounding (v_dc fixed to 0 at the terminal, with free earth-return current); r > 0 is grounding through impedance (earth current = v_dc / r). At least one grounding per connected DC island sets the signed-voltage reference.

terminal.description: Which dc_bus terminal is earthed (typically the metallic return / midpoint)

r.description: Grounding resistance [Ohm]; 0 or omitted = perfect grounding, > 0 = grounding through impedance.

dc_load.description: Constant-power DC loads connected to a dc_bus terminal pair.

terminal_map.description: DC terminals the load draws across (e.g. [pole, return]).

dc_source.description: DC-side sources (DC-coupled PV/storage feeding the DC network) connected to a dc_bus terminal pair.

terminal_map.description: DC terminals the source injects across (e.g. [pole, return]).

p.description: Active power injected [W]; fixed setpoint when p_min/p_max absent

time_series.description: Named multiplicative profiles. An element references a profile by id in its own `time_series` map, and the profile's value at step t multiplies the static value of the referenced field at step t. A profile carries no units and no absolute quantity.

additionalProperties.description: One profile. `values` is an ordered sequence of finite multiplicative factors, one per step, and the steps of every profile a case references are the same steps in the same order. There is no interpolation and no resampling: a reader evaluates the profile only at its stated steps, and a value between two steps is undefined. There are no nulls and no gaps; a step whose factor is unknown is not a profile a case may publish.

values.description: The multiplicative factors, one per step, in step order. Every entry is a number, so a null, a string, and an omitted step are all rejected, and JSON has no literal for infinity or not-a-number, so every accepted entry is finite.

items.description: Finite multiplicative factor for one step

time.description: Optional time axis, one entry per entry of `values` and in the same order: the offset in seconds of each step from the start of the case's horizon. Strictly increasing, so every step is distinct and ordered; the schema checks distinctness and a reader checks the ordering, which JSON Schema cannot state. Absent, the steps are an ordered sequence with no stated spacing.

items.description: Offset of the step from the start of the horizon [s]

configuration_type.description: Element configuration, as WYE, DELTA, or SINGLE_PHASE

terminal_map_type.description: Ordered map from the terminals of an element to the terminals of the bus it connects to. Entry i names the bus terminal the element's conductor i connects to, and fixes the conductor ordering of every per-terminal array and every matrix index of the element.

bus_type.description: bus the element is connected to

r_series_from.description: Transformer series resistance on the 'from' side [Ohm]

x_series_from.description: Transformer series reactance on the 'from' side [Ohm]

r_series_to.description: Transformer series resistance on the 'to' side [Ohm]

x_series_to.description: Transformer series reactance on the 'to' side [Ohm]

i_max_from.description: Current-magnitude limit [A] of the 'from'-side winding current, one entry per name in `terminal_map_from` and in that order. The bounded quantity is the winding current of that side, in that side's own amperes: it is never referred through the turns ratio, and each side states its own array. Position k bounds the current of winding conductor k, which for a WYE winding is the current in the conductor between bus terminal k and the winding, and for a DELTA winding is the current in coil k, which is not the terminal conductor current. An entry against a neutral terminal bounds the conductor carrying the winding's return current, and for `center_tap` the entry against the centre terminal bounds the centre-tap current, the negated sum of the two leg currents. The constraint is a magnitude circle on the complex winding current, so one entry bounds both of its components.

i_max_to.description: Current-magnitude limit [A] of the 'to'-side winding current, one entry per name in `terminal_map_to` and in that order. The bounded quantity is the winding current of that side, in that side's own amperes: it is never referred through the turns ratio, and each side states its own array. Position k bounds the current of winding conductor k, which for a WYE winding is the current in the conductor between bus terminal k and the winding, and for a DELTA winding is the current in coil k, which is not the terminal conductor current. An entry against a neutral terminal bounds the conductor carrying the winding's return current, and for `center_tap` the entry against the centre terminal bounds the centre-tap current, the negated sum of the two leg currents. The constraint is a magnitude circle on the complex winding current, so one entry bounds both of its components.

tap_ratio.description: Off-nominal ratio multiplier on the nameplate turns ratio N = v_nom_from / v_nom_to, so the effective ratio is tap_ratio * N and the ideal winding pair relates the coil voltages by that product. Default 1.0, and the start value when the ratio is a free variable. The regulator subtypes state their own `tap_ratio`, which is a regulation ratio rather than a multiplier, because a regulator has no nameplate ratio to multiply.

tap_ratio_min.description: Lower bound on `tap_ratio`. With `tap_ratio_min` strictly below `tap_ratio_max` the ratio is a free variable of the optimisation; otherwise it is fixed at `tap_ratio`.

r_neutral_from.description: Grounding resistance [Ohm] of the 'from' winding's own neutral. Absence of both neutral impedance fields adds no internal grounding branch. Explicitly zero impedance grounds that winding neutral solidly. External bus grounding remains separate.

x_neutral_from.description: Grounding reactance [Ohm] of the 'from'-side winding's own neutral; see `r_neutral_from`.

r_neutral_to.description: Grounding resistance [Ohm] of the 'to' winding's own neutral. Absence of both neutral impedance fields adds no internal grounding branch. Explicitly zero impedance grounds that winding neutral solidly. External bus grounding remains separate.

x_neutral_to.description: Grounding reactance [Ohm] of the 'to'-side winding's own neutral; see `r_neutral_to`.

g_no_load.description: No-load core-loss shunt conductance [S], stamped across the 'from'-side winding.

b_no_load.description: No-load magnetising shunt susceptance [S], stamped across the 'from'-side winding. Negative for a lagging magnetising current.

r_series.description: Transformer series resistance, defined on the wye-side winding [Ohm]

x_series.description: Transformer series reactance, defined on the wye-side winding [Ohm]

i_max_from.description: Current-magnitude limit [A] of the 'from'-side winding current, one entry per name in `terminal_map_from` and in that order. The bounded quantity is the winding current of that side, in that side's own amperes: it is never referred through the turns ratio, and each side states its own array. Position k bounds the current of winding conductor k, which for a WYE winding is the current in the conductor between bus terminal k and the winding, and for a DELTA winding is the current in coil k, which is not the terminal conductor current. An entry against a neutral terminal bounds the conductor carrying the winding's return current, and for `center_tap` the entry against the centre terminal bounds the centre-tap current, the negated sum of the two leg currents. The constraint is a magnitude circle on the complex winding current, so one entry bounds both of its components.

i_max_to.description: Current-magnitude limit [A] of the 'to'-side winding current, one entry per name in `terminal_map_to` and in that order. The bounded quantity is the winding current of that side, in that side's own amperes: it is never referred through the turns ratio, and each side states its own array. Position k bounds the current of winding conductor k, which for a WYE winding is the current in the conductor between bus terminal k and the winding, and for a DELTA winding is the current in coil k, which is not the terminal conductor current. An entry against a neutral terminal bounds the conductor carrying the winding's return current, and for `center_tap` the entry against the centre terminal bounds the centre-tap current, the negated sum of the two leg currents. The constraint is a magnitude circle on the complex winding current, so one entry bounds both of its components.

v_nom_to.description: Nominal phase-to-phase voltage of the 'to'-side winding [V]

v_nom_from.description: Nominal phase-to-phase voltage of the 'from'-side winding [V]

tap_ratio.description: Off-nominal ratio multiplier on the nameplate turns ratio N = v_nom_from / v_nom_to, so the effective ratio is tap_ratio * N and the ideal winding pair relates the coil voltages by that product. Default 1.0, and the start value when the ratio is a free variable. The regulator subtypes state their own `tap_ratio`, which is a regulation ratio rather than a multiplier, because a regulator has no nameplate ratio to multiply.

tap_ratio_min.description: Lower bound on `tap_ratio`. With `tap_ratio_min` strictly below `tap_ratio_max` the ratio is a free variable of the optimisation; otherwise it is fixed at `tap_ratio`.

r_neutral_from.description: Grounding resistance [Ohm] of the 'from' winding's own neutral. Absence of both neutral impedance fields adds no internal grounding branch. Explicitly zero impedance grounds that winding neutral solidly. External bus grounding remains separate.

x_neutral_from.description: Grounding reactance [Ohm] of the 'from'-side winding's own neutral; see `r_neutral_from`.

r_neutral_to.description: Grounding resistance [Ohm] of the 'to' winding's own neutral. Absence of both neutral impedance fields adds no internal grounding branch. Explicitly zero impedance grounds that winding neutral solidly. External bus grounding remains separate.

x_neutral_to.description: Grounding reactance [Ohm] of the 'to'-side winding's own neutral; see `r_neutral_to`.

g_no_load.description: No-load core-loss shunt conductance [S], stamped across the 'from'-side winding.

b_no_load.description: No-load magnetising shunt susceptance [S], stamped across the 'from'-side winding. Negative for a lagging magnetising current.

inverter_topology_type.description: Inverter topology: SINGLE_PHASE (2 terminals), THREE_LEG (3 terminals, no neutral current), FOUR_LEG (4 terminals, neutral current available)

prime_mover_type.description: Energy source behind the inverter: PV (non-negative, resource-limited active power), BATTERY (bidirectional), GENERIC, or STATCOM (no active source - pure reactive shunt compensator; DSTATCOM is the distribution-system alias)

dc_pole_type.description: DC terminal pole role: POSITIVE pole (v_dc > 0), NEGATIVE pole (v_dc < 0), or METALLIC_RETURN / midpoint (v_dc ~ 0)

dc_control_type.description: Converter DC-side control mode: P (constant power), V (DC-voltage master / slack), or droop (saturated V-P droop)

voltage_reference_type.description: Voltage quantity monitored by a control law

q_ref_type.description: Reactive-power limit reference: VAR_MAX (fixed Q limits) or VAR_AVAILABLE (limits scale with sqrt(s_max^2 - P^2))

p_ref_type.description: Active-power normalisation base for Volt-Watt: P_AVAILABLE, P_MAX, or S_MAX

q_unit_type.description: Unit for reactive-power limit values: VA_FRACTION (fraction of s_max) or VAR (absolute)

p_unit_type.description: Unit for active-power limit values: VA_FRACTION (fraction of s_max) or W (absolute)

regulator_type.description: ANSI step-voltage-regulator connection: A (series winding on the regulated/output side; n_eff = 1/tap_ratio) or B (series winding on the source side, standard SVR; n_eff = tap_ratio)

open_delta_connection_type.description: Open-delta phase-pair wiring (GridLAB-D convention): which two line-to-line pairs carry a regulating winding

transformer_winding.description: One winding of an n-winding transformer.

terminal_map.description: Mapping of this winding's terminals to the bus terminals

v_nom.description: Winding reference (nominal) coil voltage [V]: line-to-neutral for a WYE winding, line-to-line for a DELTA winding

r_winding.description: Winding series resistance [Ohm] on this winding's own coil base (n_ph*v_nom^2/s_rating)

delta_roll.description: DELTA only: coil rotation / vector-group sense. +1 connects coil k across phases k->k+1, -1 across k->k-1 (OpenDSS's standard delta). Ignored for WYE.

i_max.description: Current-magnitude limit [A] applied to each phase coil current of this winding, referred to this winding's own voltage. A per-coil limit, not a per-terminal one: a DELTA winding's coil current is not its terminal current.

s_rating.description: Winding rating [VA]. Defaults to the transformer s_rating when absent; the transformer s_rating remains the common short-circuit base.

tap_ratio.description: Dimensionless multiplier on this winding nominal coil voltage. Referred ideal coil voltages divide by v_nom * tap_ratio.

tap_ratio_min.description: Lower bound on this winding tap multiplier; a nonfixed interval requires a supported tap decision.

tap_ratio_max.description: Upper bound on this winding tap multiplier.

r_neutral.description: Winding-neutral-to-earth resistance [Ohm]. Absence of both neutral impedance fields adds no internal grounding branch; explicitly zero impedance gives solid grounding.

time_series_ref.description: Map from the name of a field of this element to the id of a `time_series` profile. The profile's values multiply the static value of that field, entry by entry over the profile's steps. Only a field this schema defines on this element may be named, and only a numeric one.

additionalProperties.description: Id of an entry of the top-level `time_series` table

r_series_from.description: Series-winding resistance referred to the 'from' side [Ohm]

x_series_from.description: Series-winding reactance referred to the 'from' side [Ohm]

r_series_to.description: Series resistance referred to the 'to' side [Ohm]

x_series_to.description: Series reactance referred to the 'to' side [Ohm]

tap_ratio.description: Regulation ratio (regulated/source), e.g. in [0.9, 1.1]. Default 1.0. Start value when free.

tap_ratio_min.description: Lower bound on tap_ratio. With tap_ratio_min < tap_ratio_max the tap is a free OPF variable; otherwise fixed at 'tap_ratio'.

i_max_from.description: Current-magnitude limit [A] on each conductor of the 'from' side, one entry per name in `terminal_map_from` and in that order, on the conductor between the bus terminal and the regulator and referred to that side.

i_max_to.description: Current-magnitude limit [A] on each conductor of the 'to' side, one entry per name in `terminal_map_to` and in that order, on the conductor between the bus terminal and the regulator and referred to that side.

r_series_from.description: Per-regulator series-winding resistance referred to the 'from' side [Ohm]

x_series_from.description: Per-regulator series-winding reactance referred to the 'from' side [Ohm]

r_series_to.description: Per-regulator series resistance referred to the 'to' side [Ohm]

x_series_to.description: Per-regulator series reactance referred to the 'to' side [Ohm]

tap_ratio.description: Per-regulator regulation ratios [a1, a2] (length 2). Start values when free.

tap_ratio_min.description: Per-regulator lower bounds [a1_min, a2_min]. With tap_ratio_min < tap_ratio_max (element-wise) that regulator's tap is a free OPF variable.

i_max_from.description: Current-magnitude limit [A] on each conductor of the 'from' side, one entry per name in `terminal_map_from` and in that order, on the conductor between the bus terminal and the regulator and referred to that side.

i_max_to.description: Current-magnitude limit [A] on each conductor of the 'to' side, one entry per name in `terminal_map_to` and in that order, on the conductor between the bus terminal and the regulator and referred to that side.

windings.description: Ordered list of windings; winding 1 is the reference. Length >= 2.

x_sc.description: Pairwise short-circuit reactances [Ohm], keyed "i_j" with i<j (1-based winding indices), all referred to winding 1's voltage base.

g_no_load.description: No-load (core-loss) shunt conductance [S], referenced at winding 1

b_no_load.description: No-load (magnetising) shunt susceptance [S], referenced at winding 1

description: Proposed BMOPF 0.2.0 structural schema, subject to IEEE PES BMOPF Task Force review. Electrical quantities use absolute SI units. Element IDs are table keys; ordered terminal maps establish conductor identity. Cross-field dimensions, references, role lists and bounds require semantic validation in addition to JSON Schema. Unknown electrical fields are rejected; top-level extras and meta.provenance are free-form extension locations. Neither location establishes computational support. The canonical $id identifies this schema; a case may retrieve its pinned revision from an immutable commit URL. See the proposal documentation for compatibility and implementation status.
